decision: Keep the source-lock completeness audit ACTIVE under its committed R2 tooling repair. The R1 controller rejected an extended source-lock binding before source content was read and did not run Cargo, a checker, network access or source retrieval. R2 repairs only that verifier mismatch and remains the highest-value feasible local recovery: it can characterize the precise materialization boundary without altering any frozen source. Pipeline completeness remains broader but blocked on its independent checked-object receipt-semantics protocol gate.

categories.assessment: R2 retains the finite source-materialization ledger method after a verifier-only repair. Pipeline completeness remains a broader but protocol-unready discovery method.
The R1 failure established only an audit-tooling mismatch, while the R2 ledger will create a reusable and hash-bound inventory of direct compile-time include edges in the pinned source tree.

The R2 repair is local-only and cannot support an upstream claim or external request. Pipeline completeness also has no current external action, but cannot be promoted until its local scientific gate is resolved.

R2 reuses the frozen source lock, pinned crate evidence and the preserved R1 controller error. It does not fetch or substitute any source byte. Pipeline completeness still needs a separately bound producer, adapter and receipt semantics before reuse is justified.

R2 directly removes the binding-shape blocker while retaining the exact R1 error and its conservative one source/setup inspection. Pipeline completeness remains blocked locally by its finite protocol gate.

candidates.rationale: ACTIVE under a committed R2 work record, verifier repair and exact R2 manifest. The repair separately validates the source-lock row's byte count after its path/hash binding, preserving all scientific and source inputs; the ensuing operation remains one static, local ledger only.

This remains the stronger broader conformance alternative, but no finite producer, adapter, checked-object receipt semantics, independently expected contents or fault rubric has been bound for execution.

blockers.reason: Bind the supported producer and adapters, a twelve-declaration expectation, receipt semantics, fixed faults and finite source/setup/build/tooling/process controls before promotion.
